findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-Clients resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists, the code loads the all-Clients resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the Clients resource is absent (e.g. the resource server was initialized before Clients support or the resource was not created), so the permission check throws NullPointerException instead of returning false. The String-scope overload in the same class does guard the analogous lookup, showing the missing check is an oversight; the result can be a 500 error on ordinary client view/manage/configure checks.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Clients scopes/resource
findings.body: init() returns immediately whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. Realms that already enabled FGAPv2 therefore keep a resource server created with only the Users scopes and the Users all-resource resource; the new Clients resource type, its 'Clients' all-resource resource, and the new scopes 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' are never added. Creating Clients permissions in such realms will fail (missing scopes/resources) and client permission evaluation can hit missing-resource paths, so an upgrade/migration path for existing admin-permissions clients is required.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-Clients placeholder instead of client ids
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type Clients and adds resource.getName() for granted resources. That iteration includes the all-resource resource whose name is literally 'Clients', while client-specific resources are named by client id. If the caller only has an all-Clients grant, the method returns {"Clients"} and none of the real client ids, so any consumer filtering clients by this id set will not match the clients the admin is permitted to access. Conversely it can expose a bogus identifier that is not a client. The all-resource case must be expanded to actual client ids (or excluded with callers handling the all-clients grant separately).

findings.title: Resource display names are not resolved for the Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns 'All users' for the all-resource resource and resolves a user id to a username for user-specific resources. The new Clients branch is missing, so Clients permissions fall through to resource.getDisplayName(). For the all-Clients resource that yields no meaningful 'All clients' label, and for client-specific resources whose name is the client UUID it yields the UUID/display name rather than the client's clientId. Authorization representations for Clients permissions will therefore show confusing or empty resource names in clients that consume getResourceName.
